sources.entry: pypdf - A library capable of splitting, merging, cropping, and transforming PDF pages.

summary.one_liner: pypdf is a free, open-source, pure-Python library for splitting, merging, cropping, and transforming PDF pages, and for reading text and metadata from PDFs.
summary.what_it_does: pypdf reads and writes PDF files in pure Python. It can split and merge PDFs, crop and transform pages, and add custom data, viewing options, and passwords to documents. It can extract text and metadata from PDFs. The README also mentions creating and reading annotations and encrypting and decrypting files. Optional AES encryption support is installed via a pip extra. The README points to a separate CLI tool, pdfly, that is built on pypdf, and to external documentation for further examples.
use_cases: split a PDF into separate files
add passwords or encryption to a PDF
how_to_run: pip install pypdf[crypto]  # for AES encryption/decryption
notable: Pure-Python, no external PDF engine required for core features
Can split, merge, crop and transform pages
Text and metadata extraction via PdfReader
Optional AES encryption via the pypdf[crypto] extra
Companion CLI application pdfly built on top of it
caveats: AES encryption/decryption needs the extra crypto dependencies installed separately
Pypdf 3.1.0 and above changed the API; a migration guide is referenced for older code
